# prime ideal　`def.prime-ideal`

[in graph](../#n=def.prime-ideal)　·　[Chinese page (authoritative)](./def.prime-ideal.md)

## Notes · **draft**
⭐ Examples: in $\mathbb{Z}$ both $(p)$ ($p$ prime) and $(0)$ are prime; in $K[x]$, $(f)$ is prime $\iff$ $f$ is irreducible, and $(0)$ is prime too.

⚠ A prime ideal need not be maximal: in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$, $(x)$ is prime ($\mathbb{Z}[x]/(x) \cong \mathbb{Z}$ is a domain) but not maximal.

⭐ A prime ideal is the abstraction of "divisibility": $a \in (p) \iff p \mid a$; $ab \in (p) \implies p \mid ab \implies p \mid a$ or $p \mid b$ is exactly Euclid's lemma.

> Proofs of the edges are still Chinese only: `proofs/`; the Chinese page remains authoritative.
